The ward lights dim at eleven, and that is when the real shift starts. I learned that on my second night, standing by the drugs trolley with a cold cup of tea and a list that kept growing.

## The Hours Nobody Warns You About

The middle of the night has its own weather. Phones ring less, but every call matters more. Sleep after a run of nights is hard for many nurses, and the advice I trust says to protect a fixed sleep window [[S1]].

## Small Rituals That Hold You Steady

I keep three small habits: a walk to the window at two, a proper break at four, and a handover note I write before I am tired. None of them are clever. All of them work for me.

## When The Ward Goes Quiet

Quiet is not empty. It is the time to check on the patient who stopped asking for anything.

### Key Takeaways

- Protect a fixed sleep window.
- Keep two or three small rituals.
- Write handover notes early.

By morning you will have questions about the people you hand over to, and that is where the next part of this book picks up.
